families.family: block_sparse_matmul_sdd (dense x dense -> BCSR-sparse output on given topology)
families.reference: candidate (lib ref): stk/ops/linear_ops_test.py::_mmm -> torch.mm(a,b)*to_dense(ones_like(topo)); per-block: out[i]=(a.double()@b.double())[r_i*128:(r_i+1)*128, c_i*128:(c_i+1)*128].to(a.dtype)
open_decisions: BCSR topology format: data [nnz,bs,bs] row-major blocks, row_indices/column_indices int16 (one per block), offsets int32 CSR row pointers
which output blocks are produced (only topology blocks; entries outside topology undefined/absent)
duplicate or unsorted (row,col) entries: kernel writes each listed block independently; to_dense reference scatters (last wins)
transposition of dense operands inferred from strides
accumulate fp32 (int32 for non-float dtypes) and single rounding to output dtype
spec_sources: MegaBlocks paper (Gale et al., MLSys 2023) Sec. 5.1 blocked-CSR-COO hybrid format
families.notes: grid=(nnz_blocks,); program pid reads (row_indices[pid], column_indices[pid]) and computes one 128x128 block of A@B over full K. Backward of DSD/DDS uses this kernel for the sparse-data gradient. domain: M,K,N must be multiples of 128/32/128 (asserted), no masks; rm%M wrap; out contiguous [nnz,128,128]. deviation: fp32 inputs go through tl.dot default (TF32 on sm80+); wrapper treats an operand as transposed only when both strides>1 and then swaps strides, which is wrong for general non-contiguous views (transposed views stride (1,K) are handled correctly without the flag).

families.reference: candidate (lib ref): stk/ops/linear_ops_test.py::testLinearOps_Dsd -> torch.mm(to_dense(A)[.t() if A transposed].double(), b.double()).to(b.dtype)
open_decisions: BCSR format decode (to_dense: block i placed at rows r_i*bs.., cols c_i*bs..)
transposed-sparse metadata semantics: column_indices_t/offsets_t (CSR of A^T) and block_offsets_t (index into data of original block; block read with swapped strides)
consistency requirement between row_indices/offsets/column_indices and *_t metadata (not validated)
duplicate blocks: kernel accumulates both, to_dense keeps one
block size 128 only; pid_m used directly as block row (assumes BLOCK_M==block size)
spec_sources: stk/ops/linear_ops_test.py::testLinearOps_Dsd (forward and both gradients vs torch.mm autograd)
families.notes: grid=(M/128, N/128) with swizzle2d GROUP_M=128; loops over nnz blocks of block-row pid_m in K sub-tiles of 32. Used in backward (dense grads) of SDD/DDS. domain: M,K,N multiples of 128, unmasked loads, fp16/bf16 (Matrix validation insists on fp16 data but tests use bf16). deviation: fp32 via TF32 dot; same both-strides>1 transpose heuristic on rhs as sdd.

metadata consistency and duplicate handling (not validated)
families.notes: grid=(M/128, N/128); pid_n indexes a block column of B. Used in backward of SDD/DSD. domain/deviation as dsd (multiples of 128, no masks, fp32 via TF32, both-strides>1 heuristic on lhs).
grid=(block_rows,); integer bookkeeping, exact. domain: offsets monotone non-decreasing int32 with offsets[-1]==numel(out); out int16 (column_indices dtype), so block_rows must fit int16.
